neighbours.label: 'in'/'into' introducing a plant's flowering or seasonal state ('in flower', 'in season', 'into bloom')
fire: The hillside looks spectacular in late May, when the wild lupins are in flower.
Peaches taste best when they are in season, usually from July to early September.
The cherry trees along the canal will soon be coming into bloom.
Even when it is not in flower, the shrub has attractive silver leaves.
We visited the lavender farm in July, while the fields were in full bloom.
Asparagus is cheapest when it is in season in the spring months.
The orchids in the greenhouse burst into flower almost every February.
The meadow is busy with bees when the clover is in flower.
quiet: The hillside looks spectacular in late May, when the wild lupins are tall and green.
Peaches taste best when they are ripe and soft, usually picked by hand.
The cherry trees along the canal will soon be pruned by the city gardeners.
Even when it is not watered often, the shrub keeps its attractive silver leaves.
We visited the lavender farm in July, while the fields were being harvested.
Asparagus is cheapest at the farmers' market on Saturday mornings.
The orchids in the greenhouse are repotted almost every February.
The meadow is busy with bees when the clover grows tall and thick.

notes: Card: ' in' 11 of top 32, in 'when in flower', 'when not in flower', 'when they are in season', 'coming into bloom', 'do not become sexually mature'. Opposite pole fires on plant growth descriptions; output of this pole promotes bloom/flower/heat.
